Prevention: Cassava root rot is a disease caused by various types of fungi
Select land that will not flood throughout the year and avoid water logged soil.
Avoid using planting materials from farms with reported cases of root rot diseases.
Select healthy plants for the production of planting materials, avoid plants that have wilted leaves.
Destroy plant debris (rotting stems, roots etc.) soon after harvest by burning or deep burying.
Avoid delaying the harvest of early maturing varieties.
Avoid continuous cropping on the same area of land/in infected zones, use crop rotations of at least 3 seasons with maize, millet or sorghum.
Clean farming tools after use with a 10% solution of household bleach.
Avoid planting cassava as first crop after clearance of woodland/ forests to avoid fungal attacks.
Monitoring: Monitor fields regularly for develoment of yellow mushrooms in the soil or white fruiting bodies at base of crop stems - these fungi cause root rot.
Symptoms include wilting leaves, defoliation, stem dieback and death of infected plants.
In disease endemic areas, monitor farms for single or few wilted plants growing amongst healthy plants.
Storage roots of infected plants are swollen with soft brown rot internally.
Uproot any infected plant when identified and examine roots to establish cause of wilt.
Carry out control measures at the first sign of the disease.
Direct Control: Carefully remove fruiting bodies of the fungus and destroy immediately by burning.
Isolate plants with wilt symptoms and burn, take care for disrupting any fungus.
